# Storyliner — Full Reference

> seo-keyword-storyteller.replit.app — a free tool for writing the foundational
> story of a brand in 160 characters, the length of an SEO meta description. It is
> built on nearly 2,400 years of logic from Aristotle and engineered like a Disney story,
> not decorated. A rule-based Story Coach always works offline and for free; an
> optional AI rewrite can be wired to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Authored by
> Carey Balboa, founder of IT Help San Diego Inc. ORCID 0009-0000-5237-9065.
> Part of the same body of work as The Intellectual Resistance
> (https://intellectualresistance.com/).

## The thesis

A brand begins with a single, deliberate statement — who you are, what you
believe, and the exact words a stranger would type to find you. Most people skip
it. They buy the logo and the domain first, then try to reverse-engineer a story
later, when it is expensive to change. Storyliner puts the story first and keeps
it to 160 characters so it doubles as your SEO meta description from day one.

## Operating principles

- The story is the foundation. It comes before the logo, the domain, and the ads.
- Built on Aristotle. Ethos is character — the reason you can be trusted to do
  this at all. Pathos is feeling — the reason a stranger should care for even one
  second. Logos is logic — the concrete proof that what you claim is real. A good
  story also has a shape: a hook, a turn (tension), and a payoff, even compressed
  into one breath.
- Keep it real, not buzzword soup. Under 160 characters forces honesty.

## Keywords are honest findability, not a market bet

The point is not to game or chase search. The point is to be, publicly and
consistently, who you say you are — your name, your address, and what you
actually do, identical everywhere a person or a search engine looks. When it all
lines up, you read as real, and the right people simply find you. Keywords are
not a bet on the market; they are just you, said plainly.

But honest cuts both ways. The thing you are known for may not be the thing you
wish you were known for — and that is the reality check. If it is how the world
actually finds you, it earns a slot, like it or not. The eight keywords are the
chunks that make you what you are. Name them honestly and you will rarely think
about keywords again.

## The anchor keywords (slots #1 and #2)

The first two of the eight slots are special — together they are the anchor, and
both are hand-typed rather than filled from suggestions. Slot #1 is "what you are":
your core category plus place, for example "IT support, San Diego." Slot #2 is
"who you are": your brand name. Your brand name is a keyword too (a "branded
keyword"), but a stranger who needs you does not yet know your name; they search by
the problem, not by you. Splitting the anchor into what + who makes the direction
obvious and guarantees your name has its own home, so the moment someone finds you
by category, your name binds to it. The remaining six slots are the discovery words
real strangers type at 2 a.m. — and six is really all anyone needs.

## How to choose the eight keywords

- Everything matches. Pick the one real-world name people actually call you and
  spell it identically everywhere — same spacing, same logo, colors, photos, and
  short descriptions, across your site, your listings, and every profile. You do
  not need to put "LLC" or "Inc." on everything; in fact Google discourages legal
  suffixes in your Business Profile name. Instead, place your exact registered legal
  name (the IRS version, spelling and spacing intact) where it is official: your
  website footer, your contracts, and your business registrations. That lets the
  directories that vouch for real companies match you to the official record, and
  you start to read like the bigger, established brand you are.
- The 2 a.m. test. Picture a stranger, alone in the dark, typing into a search
  bar to solve the exact problem you fix. The words they type are your keywords —
  not the words you wish they would use.
- Bread and butter. Every keyword should point at money. If a word does not lead
  someone toward becoming a customer, it is decoration — cut it.
- Name what is real. The thing you are best known for is how the world finds you,
  whether you like it or not. Keywords can be short, real phrases too — for
  example, "emergency IT help, San Diego" — not just single abstract nouns.

## Do not pay anyone to cheat

There is no shortcut around being who you say you are. Do not hire a shady PR firm
or an SEO "growth" shop to game your way up the rankings. An AI slop shop will
cheat — fake reviews, junk backlinks, machine-written filler published under your
name. Search engines catch it, and when they do the penalty lands on you: your
real listings sink and the internet's memory of your brand gets darker, not
brighter. Tell the truth clearly and let it compound; that is the only growth
that does not get taken away.

## How the tool works

- The Workshop. A 160-character story editor sits in the center, framed by eight
  keyword slots. As you write, any keyword that appears in the story lights up,
  and a live counter tracks how many you have woven in. Weave in four — your two
  anchors plus a couple of real signals, the way best practice recommends — and a
  celebration plays. You do not need all eight; cramming in keywords is stuffing,
  and stuffing is the cheating we warn against.
- Keyword suggestions. Clickable chips, sourced free from the Datamuse API, drop
  a word into the next open discovery slot. They never fill the two anchor slots
  (#1 and #2) — those are hand-typed.
- Story Coach. A free, rule-based coach scores your draft on ethos, pathos, and
  logos and checks the arc — hook, tension, payoff. It never requires an account
  or a payment and works entirely offline. A free, offline thesaurus helps tighten
  wording.
- Optional AI rewrite. Off by default; the rule-based coach always works without
  it. To enable real AI rewrites, set AI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL, and an optional
  AI_API_KEY to any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (for example, the Google Gemini
  free tier, Groq, Ollama, or LM Studio). When configured, the app exposes a
  "Get AI rewrite" action that returns two or three tips and an improved version
  under 160 characters that naturally weaves in your keywords. The AI coach is
  instructed in the same philosophy described here: face the truth, then tell it
  clearly.

## Constraints

- The story must stay at or under 160 characters (SEO meta description length).
- Exactly eight keyword slots.
- No login, no tracking, no payment required to use the core tool.
